title: Docker config.json: base64 auth value for a registry
summary: A synthetic Docker config.json whose auths map holds a base64 auth string per registry (one registry, then two registries).
rationale: The password never appears as text: it is part of the base64 of username:password. The key name auth and the registry hostname are ordinary. This is encoded embedded material (#94); the decoded username-colon-password text and its mapping back to the encoded line belong to the downstream owners.

expectation.rationale: Flag each auth value as it appears (the whole base64 string). Docker states that without a credential store it stores credentials in config.json in a base64-encoded format, and docker/cli encodes auth as base64 of username, a colon and the password. The registry key is not given a span.

sources.supports: If you don't configure a credential store, Docker stores credentials in the config.json file in a base64-encoded format. This method is less secure than configuring and using a credential store.
encodeAuth: authStr := authConfig.Username + ":" + authConfig.Password, then base64.StdEncoding.
